s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive painful skin lesions and ulcers with systemic symptoms and laboratory abnormalities
salient_findings: Progressive, painful blisters and ulcers of the groin
Enlargement of the tongue with difficulty with mastication
Numbness without weakness of the distal lower limbs
Circinate purpuric patches with erosions on the skin
Hemorrhagic flaccid bullae on the posterior perineum
Macroglossia, glossitis, and a hemorrhagic erosion on the hard palate
key_facts: 1-week history of progressive, painful blisters and ulcers of the groin
3-month history of tongue enlargement leading to difficulty with mastication
3-month history of numbness without weakness of the distal lower limbs
History of IgG λ-type multiple myeloma complicated by anemia and lytic lesions in the calvarium
Patient is taking folic acid and intramuscular cyanocobalamin supplements
Platelet count is within normal range
Prothrombin time is slightly elevated
Activated partial thromboplastin time is elevated
Serum zinc level is low
Biopsy from left groin showed subepidermal blister with chronic inflammatory infiltrate and apple-green birefringence on polarized light microscopy with Congo red staining
Direct immunofluorescence test was negative
Herpes simplex virus PCR from perineal ulcer swab was negative

shortlist.label: POEMS syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Matches the patient's symptoms of progressive painful skin lesions, ulcers, and systemic symptoms such as tongue enlargement and numbness in the lower limbs, which are consistent with the multisystem nature of POEMS syndrome

shortlist.label: bullous pemphigoid
shortlist.why_kept: Characterized by the presence of subepidermal blisters, which is consistent with the biopsy findings from the left groin, showing a subepidermal blister with chronic inflammatory infiltrate

shortlist.label: pyoderma gangrenosum
shortlist.why_kept: Presents with painful skin ulcers, which aligns with the patient's symptoms of progressive painful blisters and ulcers of the groin

shortlist.label: pemphigus vulgaris
shortlist.why_kept: Involves the formation of flaccid bullae, which could explain the hemorrhagic flaccid bullae observed on the posterior perineum

shortlist.label: vasculitis
shortlist.why_kept: Could account for the purpuric patches and macules, as well as the elevated prothrombin time and activated partial thromboplastin time, suggesting a possible vascular component to the disease

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of progressive, painful blisters and ulcers, tongue enlargement, numbness of the distal lower limbs, and history of IgG λ-type multiple myeloma are consistent with POEMS syndrome, a paraneoplastic syndrome associated with multiple myeloma. The biopsy findings of subepidermal blisters with apple-green birefringence on polarized light microscopy with Congo red staining also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: bullous pemphigoid
rejected.why: The negative direct immunofluorescence test and lack of other characteristic findings make this diagnosis less likely

rejected.label: pyoderma gangrenosum
rejected.why: The presence of subepidermal blisters and apple-green birefringence on polarized light microscopy with Congo red staining are not typical of pyoderma gangrenosum

rejected.label: pemphigus vulgaris
rejected.why: The negative direct immunofluorescence test and lack of other characteristic findings, such as flaccid bullae and oral mucosal involvement, make this diagnosis less likely

rejected.label: vasculitis
rejected.why: The lack of other characteristic findings, such as palpable purpura and systemic symptoms, make this diagnosis less likely
